ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.33 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7), representing the 3.07 km of non-exempt off-route distance at this trip's metered per-km rate; no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so detour distance flows directly into the meter and RD-2's metered branch applies: refund = Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) × this trip's per-km rate, where the rate is fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km [F4][F6]. The trace settles that the off-route segment F3 (09:24–09:30, 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km) exists and is a detour under RD-1 [F3], and that RD-4(a) does not exempt it: the only traffic records are speed bands of 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard, which are not "heavy traffic" bands 1–2 and are corroboration at most, and no traffic incidents were recorded near the route [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. The driver's statement "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is his own account written after the trip, and a GPS reroute without any reasonable cause does not satisfy the "shortest and most direct route" obligation; the driver's claim of a reroute is not route consent by the rider [F10][RD-1][RD-5].

I read the chat in full. The only messages are the rider announcing she is at the Raffles Place taxi stand with a black backpack and the driver saying he is 2 minutes away in a blue Prius [F7][F8]. Every message is timestamped and the record is complete [F9], and both were sent at 09:04–09:05, well before the off-route segment began at 09:24 [F3]. Neither message agrees to any route change, names any road or area for the diversion, or requests any stop — they are a greeting and a pickup arrangement. Thus there is no rider consent before the segment, and no rider-named stop [F7][F8][RD-5][RD-3]. The segment finding for F3 is therefore "counts", and under RD-2 it becomes a refundable detour.

Amount: the fare record gives distance_fare $34.42 over 24.41 km, i.e. $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.41008…/km [F6]. The non-exempt segment adds 3.07 km [F3], so 3.07 km × ($34.42 ÷ 24.41) = 3.07 × 1.410077 = $4.3299, rounded to $4.33 [F3][F6][RD-2]. I do not use the F4 figure ($4.51 / 3.20 km) because that is the aggregate excess-distance line for the whole trip, and RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of the unexempted segment; the rest of the +3.2 km variance (200 m-corridor drift, unmatched mileage) is not refunded [F1][F4][RD-2]. The taxable-meter components time and base are unchanged, and no ERP/toll or unpublished add-on is in the fare, so no FARE-1/FARE-2 item arises [F6][FARE-1][FARE-2].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the complaint is a fare/routing grievance and the messages are logistics [F7][F8][F10], so safety_concern is "none" and no SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 escalation is triggered [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: GPS segments, fare record and a complete timestamped chat settle every element this ruling needs [F3][F6][F9]. RD-6 is not triggered because the driver has 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but it is a no-show matter, not a route dispute, so route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 and no flag_account follows [F16][RD-6].

Under RD-5 a complete chat with no rider agreement before the segment counts, and a driver's own account that 'the GPS rerouted' made only in his post-trip statement is not rider consent [F10][RD-5]. The driver advocate requested no_action; the driver's account that the GPS rerouted him and that the meter fare stands is a post-trip statement only and is not rider consent, and no traffic incident or bands-1–2 congestion supports a reasonable-cause exemption, so the segment counts and part of the fare is refundable [F10][F11][F12][F13][RD-2][RD-4][RD-5].
